title: Capstone: 5-Module Production OTP XMPP Server
solutionExplanation: The 5-module XMPP server coordinates stream framing, stateful connection FSMs, concurrent session tables, and routing under an OTP rest_for_one supervision hierarchy. All sub-binaries are copied to prevent memory bloat, and process monitors guarantee automatic session pruning upon client disconnection.

mentalModelCheck.question: In the BeamForge XMPP Server, why is xmpp_sup configured with rest_for_one with xmpp_session_registry ordered before xmpp_router?

options.label: The router depends directly on the registry's ETS table. Under rest_for_one, if the registry crashes, the router is automatically terminated and restarted against the fresh registry, while a router crash does not kill the registry.
options.explanation: Correct! xmpp_router directly queries xmpp_session_registry's in-memory ETS table. If the registry crashed under one_for_one, the router would hold dead table handles. Under rest_for_one, downstream router is restarted cleanly, but upstream registry is safe if router crashes.

options.label: rest_for_one is the only supervisor strategy that supports gen_statem processes.
options.explanation: All OTP supervisor strategies support any worker behaviour (gen_server, gen_statem, etc.).

options.label: The router requires higher CPU priority than the registry.
options.explanation: Supervisor child order defines startup sequence and crash restart cascades, not BEAM CPU priority.
